annotation.title_clean: The Civil Aviation [(No. 19) Unmanned Aircraft Systems] Regulations, 2016
annotation.title_en: The Civil Aviation [(No. 19) Unmanned Aircraft Systems] Regulations, 2016
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Civil Aviation Authority of Trinidad and Tobago (with approval of the Minister of Works and Transport)
annotation.venue: Trinidad and Tobago Gazette, Legal Supplement Part B, Legal Notice No. 183
annotation.summary_en: Trinidad and Tobago's 2016 binding regulations on unmanned aircraft systems, made under the Civil Aviation Act. They set weight-based UA categories and require registration, operator certificates and licences, airworthiness checks, visual line of sight operation, no-fly zones and altitude limits, accident reporting, and insurance for commercial use. They also set club rules and penalties.
key_provisions_or_claims: UAS must be registered with the Civil Aviation Authority; commercial operators need an Operator Certificate and category-specific licences
Five UA categories by mass and speed, with operator licensing tied to category
Visual line of sight required; BVLOS only by Authority approval; one operator or observer per UAS
Altitude and distance limits near aerodromes; no flights over persons, private or public property without consent or permission
Public liability insurance required for commercial operations; accidents must be reported within ten days; fine of TT$350,000 and five years' imprisonment for endangering aviation or property
